name: Zinc oxide mineral makeup

card.summary: A mineral makeup base built on zinc oxide that evens and covers skin while also filtering UVA and UVB, helping protect against sun-driven ageing and uneven tone.
card.note: Makeup coverage is thin compared with a sunscreen layer, so SPF labelling and application amount matter.

quick.overview:
Zinc oxide mineral makeup is a powder or foundation whose main ingredient is zinc oxide, listed on labels as CI 77947. It evens skin tone and soaks up shine, and zinc oxide is also a UV filter.

That combination is the appearance payoff: coverage now, plus protection against the sun exposure that drives uneven pigmentation and visible ageing. Wikipedia describes zinc oxide as the broadest spectrum UVA and UVB absorber and notes that it is photostable.
quick.how: It is applied like other powder or liquid base products, typically over moisturiser or sunscreen. Some users choose it for sensitive skin, since zinc oxide is described as nonirritating and non-comedogenic.
quick.risks: Zinc oxide itself is considered low-toxicity on skin. Inhaling loose powder can irritate airways, and mineral makeup may leave a white cast on deeper skin tones unless it is micronised or tinted.

lead: Zinc oxide mineral makeup uses zinc oxide as its base pigment and filler. On ingredient lists the compound appears as CI 77947, and Wikipedia identifies it as a main ingredient of mineral makeup [1].

People use it for two linked reasons: it evens skin tone, and zinc oxide absorbs UV. The same article says zinc oxide is the broadest spectrum UVA and UVB absorber and is completely photostable. The US FDA approves it as a sunscreen ingredient [1].

Many sun products use nanoparticle zinc oxide so the film does not look white. Wikipedia reports that nanoparticles are not absorbed into the body beyond the outer skin layer, though a small amount of zinc is absorbed [1].

chain: Zinc oxide base applied to skin
Less sun-driven uneven tone over time
angle.text: The product evens how skin looks immediately and adds some UV filtering, which is relevant to the pigmentation and ageing sunlight causes.

paras: Zinc oxide is also the active component of calamine lotion and appears in baby powder and barrier creams [1]. In mineral makeup it provides colour, opacity and UV filtering in one ingredient.
Wikipedia describes zinc oxide as absorbing UV across both the UVA (320 to 400 nm) and UVB (280 to 320 nm) ranges, and as photostable [1].

The oxide is described as non-toxic, and the FDA lists it as generally recognised as safe as a food additive. The hazard noted is inhaling fumes from heated zinc [1]. In one formulation finding, UV degraded small-molecule absorbers combined with zinc oxide, and those mixtures were toxic in zebrafish embryos [1].
No studies found. Zinc oxide as a sunscreen ingredient is described more broadly in the encyclopedia source [1].

timeline.event: Zinc white is accepted as an oil-painting pigment, later partly replacing lead white [1].
